prohibited_recommendations: Do not diagnose MS based on non-specific white-matter lesions alone without meeting the 2024 revised McDonald criteria and excluding mimics
Do not attribute the earlier left leg episode or the current symptoms to stress or a functional disorder
Do not start a platform therapy (interferon-beta, glatiramer acetate, teriflunomide) as first treatment for this highly active disease
Do not start natalizumab given the anti-JCV antibody index of 2.84 when an anti-CD20 alternative is available, and never without an explicit PML benefit-risk discussion
Do not administer live-attenuated vaccines (MMR, live varicella-zoster, yellow fever, oral typhoid) after starting ocrelizumab, ofatumumab or cladribine
Do not use chronic oral corticosteroids as maintenance treatment for MS: they do not prevent relapses or disability and cause cumulative harm
Do not use CT of the brain in place of gadolinium-enhanced MRI to characterise lesion burden and activity
required_recommendations: State relapsing-remitting MS by the 2024 McDonald criteria, naming the regions that give DIS (periventricular, juxtacortical, infratentorial, spinal cord and right optic nerve: 5 of 5, so DIT is not required), with the right optic neuritis 18 months ago and the left leg episode 11 months ago as earlier attacks.

Treat the current disabling relapse with IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 3-5 days after a urine dipstick and culture exclude infection, stopping as-needed ibuprofen or adding a proton pump inhibitor during the pulse; plasma exchange if there is no response.
Measure the post-void residual volume and treat urgency with an antimuscarinic or intermittent self-catheterisation according to the residual.

Offer high-efficacy disease-modifying therapy through the MS specialist team for highly active disease (three attacks in 18 months with incomplete recovery, 14 T2 lesions with 4 enhancing, an active cord lesion), preferring an anti-CD20 antibody (ocrelizumab or ofatumumab) over natalizumab given the anti-JCV index of 2.84, after discussing pregnancy plans and contraception.
Use the completed pre-treatment serology (HBsAg, anti-HBc, HCV, HIV negative; VZV immune), complete non-live vaccinations before the first anti-CD20 dose and give no live vaccines during treatment.
Continue vitamin D replacement and adjust the dose (25-OH vitamin D 26 ng/mL on 2000 IU daily).

patient.history_present_illness: Ms. Sofia Reyes is a 24-year-old right-handed woman of Hispanic descent who presented to the neurology inpatient service with a 3-week history of worsening right leg weakness, sensory disturbance in the right side, and new urinary urgency. She reports that her symptoms began approximately 21 days ago when she noticed heaviness and stiffness in her right leg that has progressively worsened to the point of affecting her gait and causing her to nearly fall twice. Over the past week she has developed mild bilateral lower extremity stiffness. She endorses a tight, band-like burning sensation around her mid-abdomen at the T8 level, intermittent and worsened by exertion. She also has urinary urgency with rare urge incontinence, which she finds socially distressing. She notes that hot showers transiently worsen both the leg weakness and a persistent hazy quality to her right-eye vision — the latter she attributes to a prior episode of 'optic nerve inflammation' 18 months ago from which she never fully recovered. On detailed questioning she recalls a second distinct episode approximately 11 months ago, during which she experienced left leg weakness and an unsteady gait lasting about 3 weeks; this episode was evaluated at urgent care and attributed to 'stress-related functional overlay'; no MRI was performed at that time and the symptoms partially resolved but did not fully remit. She reports persistent fatigue that she describes as a 'heaviness' distinct from her prior normal tiredness. She denies new visual loss, diplopia, dysphagia, arm weakness, cognitive changes, fever, weight loss, oral ulcers, joint pain, or skin rash. She has a family history notable for her mother having multiple sclerosis. She has not had any vaccinations in the past year. She is sexually active and uses oral contraception. She has no prior MS diagnosis and has never been on any disease-modifying therapy.
